title: Wringer fleet event
description: ONE LINE of `fleet.jsonl`, not the file. Append-only, one JSON object per line, every line carrying `prev_hash` — the sha256 of the line before it, or 64 zeros for the first — so the ledger is tamper-evident on its own terms. Every string value is scrubbed by the redactor before it is written. Absence is meaningful throughout: a key appears only in the case it describes.

ts.description: Local ISO-8601 with offset, millisecond precision — fine enough to order two fast events, coarse enough to stay readable.

prev_hash.description: sha256 of the previous line, or 64 zeros for the first. Makes the LEDGER tamper-evident and says nothing about the rest of the bundle — that is `digests.json`'s job.

oneOf.title: task.worktree
oneOf.description: Only when `worktree: true`. The only git WRITE a fleet performs, and it is metadata — `worktree add` and `worktree remove`, never a commit or a branch move.

fallback.description: Present only from attempt 2, and only when `fleet.worker_fallbacks` declares a rung for it. The self-healing ladder is a declared escalation, so which rung ran is evidence rather than a detail.

oneOf.title: task.parked
oneOf.description: A task that will not be retried, and why. `deterministic` is the important one: the same failure signature twice means retrying would repeat it, which is the lesson of the incident this supervision layer was built after.

oneOf.title: task.reaped
oneOf.description: A child killed for making no progress — liveness measured by ledger growth, not by a process still existing.

loop.description: The loop bundle this task produced, or null when the child wrote none.

failure_signature.description: Present only when the child's last `verify.finished` carried one. Two identical signatures are what the breaker refuses to retry.

oneOf.title: task.finished — exhausted with on_exhausted: fail
oneOf.description: A THIRD shape under the same `type`, with a disjoint key set: no status, no reason, no loop. Modelled rather than tidied — `wringer.fleet.v1` froze at v0.2.0 and describes what the code writes, not what would have been neater.
